groups.name: Rain
groups.blurb: weather on the other side of the glass

groups.name: Fire
groups.blurb: something burning slowly in the room

groups.name: Wind
groups.blurb: air moving through a place you are not

groups.name: Night
groups.blurb: the hours when the world gets quiet

groups.name: Room
groups.blurb: the small machinery of being indoors

groups.name: Travel
groups.blurb: moving, with nowhere to be yet

sounds.name: Light Rain
sounds.note: Pink noise shaped to the spectrum of falling water, with individual drops scattered on top.

sounds.name: Downpour
sounds.note: The same bed, widened and weighted, at four times the drop density.

sounds.name: Rain on Glass
sounds.note: Rain heard from inside, with everything above 1.4 kHz taken away by the wall.

sounds.name: Rain on Canvas
sounds.note: A stretched surface rings at a pitch when you hit it. That resonance is why a tent sounds nothing like grass.

sounds.name: Rain in Leaves
sounds.note: Brighter and more scattered, each drop landing on something that gives.

sounds.name: Distant Thunder
sounds.note: A roll every forty seconds or so, at random. Occasionally it lands close.

sounds.name: Campfire
sounds.note: A breathing low roar, fine ticking, and the odd pop that splits into splinters.

sounds.name: Low Wind
sounds.note: Gusts driven by a random walk, so the wind gets brighter as it gets louder.

sounds.name: Mountain Wind
sounds.note: Thin air over bare rock. No low body at all, which is the whole difference from the one above.

sounds.name: Blizzard
sounds.note: Hard gusts with fine ice driven against the surface you are sheltering behind.

sounds.name: Leaves
sounds.note: Thousands of small ticks whose density rises and falls with the gust.

sounds.name: Wind Chimes
sounds.note: Inharmonic tube partials in a major pentatonic, rung in clusters when the wind catches them.

sounds.name: Ocean
sounds.note: A nine second swell that drifts over minutes, with foam that only appears at the crest.

sounds.name: Stream
sounds.note: Bright moving water, with resonant filter sweeps standing in for bubbles.

sounds.name: Rapids
sounds.note: The same river in a hurry. Far more churn, and a low bed underneath it.

sounds.name: Waterfall
sounds.note: Mass of falling water surges rather than sitting still, and the spray brightens as it does.

sounds.name: Underwater
sounds.note: Everything above 320 Hz gone, with bubbles rising in little clusters.

sounds.name: Cave Drips
sounds.note: A drip is a pitch that rises as the cavity it made closes up. The space answers each one.

sounds.name: Crickets
sounds.note: Seven insects, each with its own pitch, position and tempo, interfering with each other.

sounds.name: Cicadas
sounds.note: A carrier buzzing near 5 kHz, amplitude modulated in the tens of hertz. The modulation is the insect.

sounds.name: Frogs
sounds.note: Six throats around a pond, each with its own pulse rate. Pulse rate sets the species as much as pitch.

sounds.name: Owls
sounds.note: Nearly a pure tone with a breathy edge, in answering pairs, about three times a minute.

sounds.name: Cafe
sounds.note: Seven synthetic talkers, cups, and an espresso machine that fires now and then. No two minutes are ever the same.

sounds.name: Restaurant
sounds.note: Eleven voices, far more crockery, and people interrupting each other.

sounds.name: Bar
sounds.note: Fourteen voices, short phrases, and a laugh every twenty seconds or so.

sounds.name: Market
sounds.note: Open air, so nothing is muffled and the voices carry further apart.

sounds.name: Office
sounds.note: Four people, mostly not talking, over a lot of air handling.

sounds.name: Through a Wall
sounds.note: All the rhythm of speech and none of the consonants. The most useful of these for actually working.

sounds.name: Library
sounds.note: Two people who will say something roughly twice a minute, and otherwise the room itself.

sounds.name: Singing Bowl
sounds.note: Five inharmonic partials with staggered decays, struck about twice a minute.

sounds.name: Temple Bell
sounds.note: Eight partials over a very low hum tone, the longest of them ringing for half a minute.

sounds.name: Gong
sounds.note: Twenty two inharmonic partials that bloom upward for a second or two after the strike before they fade.

sounds.name: Shishi-odoshi
sounds.note: The bamboo fills, tips, knocks the stone, and pours itself out.

sounds.name: Bamboo Flute
sounds.note: Long notes from a minor pentatonic with wide silences. The breath across the edge is half the instrument.

sounds.name: Rainstick
sounds.note: Grains falling past pins, thinning out and then turned over again.

sounds.name: Low Drone
sounds.note: Root, fifth and octave, detuned and drifting, so the beating never settles into a pattern.

sounds.name: Open Drone
sounds.note: The same idea an octave up, where it stops being a floor and starts being a room.

sounds.name: Soft Keys
sounds.note: A laptop board. Almost no switch, mostly the dull sound of the case taking the hit.

sounds.name: Tactile Keys
sounds.note: A bump you can hear but not a click. The middle of the three, and the one most people actually type on.

sounds.name: Clicky Keys
sounds.note: Two clicks per press: the switch, then the click jacket an instant later, up at 5 kHz.

sounds.name: Thocky Keys
sounds.note: Low and round. The bottom-out is the loudest part, which is the whole point of the build.

sounds.name: Typewriter
sounds.note: Hammers on a platen, a margin bell at the end of every line, and the carriage thrown back by hand.

sounds.name: Writing
sounds.note: Short strokes with thinking pauses between them, and a page turned every half minute.

sounds.name: Clock
sounds.note: Tick and tock are different sounds. The escapement hits two different pallets, and a real pendulum is never quite even.

sounds.name: Fan
sounds.note: Three detuned saws beating against each other under a bed of moving air.

sounds.name: Refrigerator
sounds.note: Mains hum and its harmonics over a motor that cycles on and off across several minutes.

sounds.name: Washing Machine
sounds.note: The drum turns one way, pauses, and turns back. Everything else follows that.

sounds.name: Kettle
sounds.note: Forty bubbles a second against a resonant metal body, and steam on top.

sounds.name: Heartbeat
sounds.note: Lub then dub, two valve closures rather than one beat, drifting with the breath between 52 and 72.

sounds.name: Cabin
sounds.note: The low, enveloping drone of being in transit with nowhere to be.

sounds.name: Train
sounds.note: Rail joints come in pairs because each carriage has two bogies, and the carriages are all the same length.

sounds.name: Traffic
sounds.note: Each vehicle sweeps across the stereo field and brightens as it draws level with you.

sounds.name: White
sounds.note: Equal power at every frequency. The loudest-feeling of the colours.

sounds.name: Pink
sounds.note: Equal power per octave, which is what most people actually mean by white noise.

sounds.name: Brown
sounds.note: Deeper still. Closest to a distant waterfall, and the kindest over long hours.

sounds.name: Green
sounds.note: Energy gathered around 500 Hz, near the centre of hearing. Masks speech better than any of the others.

sounds.name: Blue
sounds.note: Tilted upward, all air. Good against a clattering keyboard, hard going for long.

sounds.name: Cafe Room
sounds.note: A real room with real people in it, recorded in Norway. The counterpart to the synthesised cafe above.

sounds.name: Restaurant Room
sounds.note: Recorded by Félix Blume, who spends his life pointing microphones at places.

sounds.name: Coffee Shop
sounds.note: Cups, the machine, and a low ceiling.

sounds.name: Bazaar
sounds.note: An open market in Palestine. Voices carry differently with no roof over them.

sounds.name: Library Room
sounds.note: Mostly the building. Someone moves about once a minute.

sounds.name: Cathedral
sounds.note: A very large stone room doing nothing at all, which turns out to be a sound.

sounds.name: Temple Bells
sounds.note: Recorded bronze, for when the synthesised bell is too clean.

sounds.name: Chimes Outside
sounds.note: Real tubes in a real garden, with the garden audible behind them.

sounds.name: Blizzard Outside
sounds.note: The recorded version. Harsher and less even than the synthesised one.

sounds.name: Fireplace
sounds.note: A proper hearth with logs in it, two minutes of it.

sounds.name: Thunderstorm
sounds.note: Rain and thunder together, as they actually arrive.

sounds.name: Harbour
sounds.note: Water against stone, boats, and gulls who have opinions.

sounds.name: Forest Brook
sounds.note: A small stream with trees over it.

sounds.name: Forest at Night
sounds.note: What a forest does when nobody is in it.

sounds.name: Dawn Chorus
sounds.note: The half hour before sunrise, when every bird decides to speak at once.

sounds.name: Birds
sounds.note: A second chorus, further off and less busy.

sounds.name: Frogs at Night
sounds.note: A real pond, which is messier than the synthesised one and better for it.

sounds.name: Train Carriage
sounds.note: Inside a moving carriage. The joints are not as even as the synthesised ones.

sounds.name: Subway Station
sounds.note: Platform, tunnel, and the air they push ahead of them.

sounds.name: City Street
sounds.note: Traffic with buildings on both sides of it.

sounds.name: Airport
sounds.note: A terminal at Seattle. Announcements, distance, and nothing to do.

sounds.name: Airplane Cabin
sounds.note: The recorded cabin, with passengers in it.

sounds.name: Pages
sounds.note: Someone else reading a physical book, slowly.

sounds.name: Pencil
sounds.note: Graphite on paper, which sounds nothing like a pen.

sounds.name: Wall Clock
sounds.note: A real escapement, with all the unevenness that implies.

sounds.name: Washer
sounds.note: A full cycle, recorded from the next room.

sounds.name: Fridge Hum
sounds.note: One compressor, running.

presets.name: Deep Work
presets.blurb: rain, a fan, and someone else typing

presets.name: Hearth
presets.blurb: a fire going while it rains outside

presets.name: Third Place
presets.blurb: a cafe you are not expected to talk in

presets.name: Temple Garden
presets.blurb: bamboo, bowl and a little wind

presets.name: Shore
presets.blurb: the sea doing what it always does

presets.name: Late Night
presets.blurb: crickets, a far off storm, lofi underneath

presets.name: In Transit
presets.blurb: a train, and the weather going past

presets.name: Summer Afternoon
presets.blurb: cicadas, chimes, and nothing to do

presets.name: Deep Forest
presets.blurb: a stream, leaves, and rain somewhere above

presets.name: Nothing Much
presets.blurb: brown noise and a clock, for when anything else is too much

presets.name: Underground
presets.blurb: drips in a hard empty space

presets.name: Nocturne
presets.blurb: strings and a voice, over rain
